default.notes: Default is unattached CLI and unloaded desktop sessions. k kills only the focused row independently of multi-selection marks through guarded close dispatch; keep the picker open and remove successfully closed rows from cached views without rediscovery, preserving query, filters and other marks on both supported fzf versions. Failed or canceled closes keep their row and report the outcome. Killing the last row leaves an empty picker until cancellation, never starting a session. Ctrl-F opens staged filter settings for State and every session column: agent, progress, interface, model, host, repository, session/slot, context and task. Enter chooses values; Apply filters commits and enables them. Esc in a nested picker keeps its value; Esc in settings discards staged edits. Reset filters to defaults stages unattached and clears columns. Ctrl-A disables filters without changing saved choices; Ctrl-L restores them. --attached starts with filters off and defaults retained. One highlighted ON/OFF summary replaces per-facet hotkeys; narrow headers show selected column count and settings retains full values. Progress follows the displayed continued-work marker, not current computation or completion. Search is preserved and hidden marks removed. Snapshot scope, action semantics, compact rows and selection gutter remain unchanged. No LAST TURN, preview, or new-session controls.

default.notes: Ctrl-F opens staged filter settings for state, agent, host/origin and repository; close includes interface. Apply enables saved choices; nested cancellation keeps values and settings cancellation discards edits. Reset stages default state and cleared columns. Ctrl-A disables filters; Ctrl-L restores saved choices. One highlighted ON/OFF summary replaces individual facet hotkeys. Filtering preserves search and removes hidden marks without discovery or scope expansion. Unavailable registered hosts warn and are skipped; discovery retains local and reachable rows. SSH failures report status and bounded terminal-safe stderr without asserting host downtime; scanner stdin is disconnected. Saved resumes retain local locks and known-owner checks, but cannot verify ownership on unavailable hosts. Local scan failures remain fatal. Default order is actual last user turn newest first, unknown times last, without pinning live rows. Alt-T last turn, Alt-R repository, Alt-G agent, Alt-O host/origin, Alt-V session select immutable snapshot sorting; text modes ascend with newest turn and stable identity ties and natural numeric session slots. Filter settings, reset and on/off preserve the selected sort; Alt-T restores last-turn sorting. Search preserves the selected order. Narrow headers use ^ Ctrl and M Alt. Saved metadata refreshes on registered hosts by repository identity by default; --remote remains compatible. Canonical and verified renamed roots and swept rollouts are included. Exact IDs determine live ownership; independent saved conversations in occupied slots use guarded fresh allocation. Only selected transcripts are fetched. All-repository discovery includes repositories registered only on a reachable host and orphan Codex rollouts with exact Git metadata, even without local registrations. Metadata browsing and cancellation never clone or register repositories. Only a selected saved identity may create its guarded local checkout. GitHub transfers match only authenticated immutable repository IDs; selected different-name identities require fresh proof. Rows begin with explicit cached PR state badges. Alt-M toggles hiding only explicitly MERGED rows, enabling filters; Ctrl-A disables and Ctrl-L restores this choice, Reset clears it. Multiple associated PRs must all be merged; mixed, unknown and no-PR rows remain. Short headers use M-M -merged to hide and M-M +merged to show. State is immutable snapshot metadata, never inferred from task text.

session resume.notes: Terminal launches run without echoing internal shell commands or exit instructions; agent output and diagnostics remain visible. Saved Codex resume resolves unindexed held sibling locks through validated session_meta workspace identity in active and archived rollouts. A still-unassociated exact lock is inspected through bounded lock-holder open rollout metadata; process cwd and other thread IDs never establish unrelatedness. Unknown, invalid or unreadable evidence fails closed; ownership refusals identify the conversation and verified PIDs with finish/exit recovery and a concise retry diagnostic, without process arguments or a traceback. Confirmed missing/invalid GitHub authentication warns once per affected host before selection, including empty and automatic results, without blocking available conversations; persistent compact picker warning survives filter/sort/reset/all. Remedy: gh auth login --hostname github.com on the named host. Network/rate-limit/permission failures and missing gh do not trigger auth warnings. Cross-host policy: Claude defaults to t transfer; Codex defaults to manual native desktop Hand off (no supported CLI adapter). Agent settings show/persist the effective mechanism and explicit Codex t override. Native returns nonzero with app steps before transfer mutations; local resume and remote attach unchanged. Batch failures stop on the first error or cancellation, print a final identity/reason/retry/ready/not-attempted summary, and never attach over failures. Tab failures retain successful sessions and exit nonzero.

version.notes: Preserve the release/revision first line; label the actual executable Source and current Git Worktree with absolute paths and branches, even when they differ. Packaged sources say release; detached checkouts say detached HEAD; outside Git is explicit. Escape control characters. Resolve metadata only on request, with no configuration load, network, picker, or update prompt.

first_run.notes: Resolve native agent executables outside PATH for reviewed login steps; failed steps remain resumable. Choice q/Esc navigates back with current selections retained; review n/Esc returns to the last applicable choice. Review q, welcome q/Esc, and Ctrl-C cancel. Empty steps are skipped; completed GitHub install/login is not repeated. Agent sign-in uses a separate optional checklist with no initial marks; skipping sign-in still allows installation. Only chosen sign-ins run after review. Authenticated agents have compact logged-in labels in agent selection, read-only context beside remaining login choices, and an Already logged in summary in review; they never become selectable login actions. After reviewed registration is saved, offer Verify SSH now or Later for distinct added or changed target strings. Native OpenSSH owns the restored terminal and asks for host fingerprint confirmation; never auto-accept trust. Refused/unavailable checks warn and continue, preserving registration. Ctrl-C stops with 130 and retains saved changes; alias/default-only edits never connect.

returning.notes: Choose an existing registered checkout or rerun discovery; reuse session ownership checks.

advisories_opt_in.notes: Only T_VULNERABILITY_CHECK=1: print bounded cached repository-tool findings to stderr and schedule a detached refresh; never block on probes/network or remediate.

bare_t.notes: Interactive startup optionally displays cached repository-tool advisories and schedules detached refresh when T_VULNERABILITY_CHECK=1; nonterminal bare t stays side-effect free.

help_style.summary: Quick command reference; explanations belong in structured t help topics.

color.scope: all quick and detailed help, including agent support and compatibility aliases
color.enabled: stdout is a TTY; NO_COLOR absent; TERM != dumb; CLICOLOR != 0
color.layout: ANSI-stripped colored output exactly equals plain output, including newlines; style after wrapping

terminal_titles.label: Bounded public command words; remote SSH actions add host, never worker code or delegated payloads.
terminal_titles.cleanup: Clear on normal return, error and cancellation; preserve handler exit status and caller cwd changes.
terminal_titles.quiet: Redirected stdout, TERM=dumb, internal workers and machine output emit no OSC.
